UnfairPlay

UnfairPlay recovers a FairPlay model from an enrolled Mac and uses it to
decrypt personalized iOS IPAs. It is a standalone Go program.

It does not log in to Apple, buy apps, or download IPAs. You can use ipatool or
another downloader for that part.

 Legal and ethical use

Use UnfairPlay only with apps you lawfully acquired and accounts and devices
you control. It is intended for interoperability, preservation, and authorized
research. The authors do not condone piracy, credential theft, copyright
infringement, or unauthorized distribution of decrypted apps.

 Discord

Project discussion and support: UnfairPlay Discord.

Unsupported, incomplete, symlinked, or already-decrypted bundles fail closed.

The installed app and IPA must be the same app and belong to the same Store
enrollment. An explicit IPA takes precedence; failed validation never triggers
an automatic retry using the installed bundle.

Recovery still authenticates the selected SINF and requires complete archive
decryption before saving a model. Reports identify validation source as
 installed-app or provided . A reconstructed validation archive describes the
installed variant, not the original Store download or any omitted architectures.

Large enrollment databases print bounded recovery progress to standard error.
The final JSON result remains on standard output.

The setup result includes plaintext verified for the validation archive.
A successful setup can report false when any decrypted image lacks
pre-encryption hashes; this is separate from whether the model was recovered
and saved successfully.

 Export enrollment now, choose an IPA later

On an already enrolled Mac, export the enrollment without supplying an installed
app or IPA:

 

The output parent directory must already exist. The command never overwrites an
existing snapshot. It writes a mode-0600 file and restores its ownership to the
invoking user when run through sudo.

The snapshot contains the hardware identity and one distinct supported SIDB
container. Export authenticates and decodes the container, but does not select
an account/key route or produce a validated model. It neither enrolls the Mac
nor adds missing licenses. Treat it as broader private enrollment state: keep it
secret and transfer it only to machines you control, preserving mode 0600.

Later, on macOS or Linux, select a personalized IPA and run setup as your normal
user:

 

This uses the IPA's own licenses; no installed-app path is required. Setup
authenticates the exact selected route and signed page-key envelopes, then
decrypts and validates the complete IPA before installing the usual reusable
model. Missing pre-encryption hashes remain plaintext verified=false .
Snapshot setup currently requires every encrypted image in the IPA to share
one user/key selector; multiple-selector IPAs reject explicitly. A snapshot can
be reused with different IPAs or selectors already present in its captured
state. Missing records require an appropriate enrollment; recovery never tries
other routes. Re-export after enrollment changes when necessary.

saved models continue to work. Synthetic tests cover this workflow; private
installed-app versus snapshot equivalence is an opt-in control in QA.md.

intro.html:
UnfairPlay recovers a FairPlay model from an enrolled Mac and uses it to decrypt personalized iOS IPAs. It is a standalone Go program.

It does not log in to Apple, buy apps, or download IPAs. You can use ipatool or another downloader for that part.

install.title: Do I need to run setup for every app?
install.html: No. One model can decrypt different IPAs personalized for the same enrollment. Each app still has its own key inside its personalized SINF.

usage.title: Usage
usage.html:
First, sign in to the native Mac App Store. Install an iPhone or iPad app and open it once. Set up reusable decryption from that installed app:

sudo ./unfairplay setup --app /Applications/App.app

No separate IPA download is needed when the installed bundle contains supported encrypted images and their matching licenses. Setup and collect build a private validation archive from the complete inner iOS bundle, preserving its bytes. Unsupported, incomplete, symlinked, or already-decrypted bundles fail closed.

To validate against a downloaded IPA instead, pass --ipa explicitly:

sudo ./unfairplay setup --app /Applications/App.app --ipa App.ipa

The installed app and IPA must be the same app and belong to the same Store enrollment. An explicit IPA takes precedence; failed validation never triggers an automatic retry using the installed bundle.

Recovery still authenticates the selected SINF and requires complete archive decryption before saving a model. Reports identify validation_source as installed-app or provided. A reconstructed validation archive describes the installed variant, not the original Store download or any omitted architectures.

Large enrollment databases print bounded recovery progress to standard error. The final JSON result remains on standard output.

The setup result includes plaintext_verified for the validation archive. A successful setup can report false when any decrypted image lacks pre-encryption hashes; this is separate from whether the model was recovered and saved successfully.

The saved model is private. It is tied to the Mac App Store enrollment, not to one app, so it can decrypt other personalized IPAs from the same enrollment. Back it up only in encrypted storage and never share it.

Decrypt another IPA:

./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa

The default model directory is inside the user configuration directory. Set UNFAIRPLAY_MODEL_DIR or pass --model to use another location.

Export enrollment now, choose an IPA later

On an already enrolled Mac, export the enrollment without supplying an installed app or IPA:

sudo ./unfairplay export-enrollment --output enrollment.snapshot

The output parent directory must already exist. The command never overwrites an existing snapshot. It writes a mode-0600 file and restores its ownership to the invoking user when run through sudo.

The snapshot contains the hardware identity and one distinct supported SIDB container. Export authenticates and decodes the container, but does not select an account/key route or produce a validated model. It neither enrolls the Mac nor adds missing licenses. Treat it as broader private enrollment state: keep it secret and transfer it only to machines you control, preserving mode 0600.

Later, on macOS or Linux, select a personalized IPA and run setup as your normal user:

./unfairplay setup --enrollment enrollment.snapshot --ipa App.ipa
./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa

This uses the IPA's own licenses; no installed-app path is required. Setup authenticates the exact selected route and signed page-key envelopes, then decrypts and validates the complete IPA before installing the usual reusable model. Missing pre-encryption hashes remain plaintext_verified=false. Snapshot setup currently requires every encrypted image in the IPA to share one user/key selector; multiple-selector IPAs reject explicitly. A snapshot can be reused with different IPAs or selectors already present in its captured state. Missing records require an appropriate enrollment; recovery never tries other routes. Re-export after enrollment changes when necessary.

--app and --enrollment are mutually exclusive. Existing app-based setup and saved models continue to work. Synthetic tests cover this workflow; private installed-app versus snapshot equivalence is an opt-in control in QA.md.

Decryption behavior

IPAs with extensions and watch apps are decrypted in one pass.

The output keeps the input's SC_Info licenses and iTunesMetadata.plist, which identify the Store account. To create a redacted copy for private analysis or authorized collaboration, add --strip-account-data: it omits every SC_Info member and removes the Apple ID and purchaser fields from iTunesMetadata.plist. Redaction does not authorize redistributing the app; the legal and ethical use terms above still apply. Test without keeping plaintext with:

./unfairplay verify --input AnotherApp.ipa

The decryption path handles ARMv6/Thumb-1, ARMv7, ARM64, and ARM64_32/watchOS slices. Available pre-encryption page hashes must match; a mismatch fails closed. Older executables without these tables can decrypt, but report plaintext_verified=false.

Run a decrypted IPA on an Apple silicon Mac

After decryption, build a locally signed app:

./unfairplay convert-decrypted-ipa-macos \
  --input App.decrypted.ipa \
  --output App.macos.app
open App.macos.app

Run conversion on an Apple silicon Mac with /usr/bin/codesign available. No enrollment model is needed for this step. The default output is <input-stem>.macos.app; the destination must not already exist.

The command selects generic arm64 slices, retargets their loader metadata to Mac Catalyst, fixes the Swift UIKit library path when present, updates the main bundle metadata, and ad-hoc signs executable files and nested bundles. Load-command growth requires bounded, unused header padding. It retains the app's minimum binary OS requirement with a Catalyst 14.0 floor. This loader approach is also used by PlayCover.

The output removes Store licenses, provisioning profiles, stale bundle signatures, and Watch apps. It uses fresh sandbox entitlements for outgoing network connections and user-selected files. Original account entitlements, push notifications, app groups, keychain groups, and iCloud access are not preserved. Symlinks, conflicting archive names, encrypted images, 32-bit-only images, and arm64e-only images are rejected.

This is a compatibility conversion, not a rebuild from source. Apps can still fail because of unavailable iOS APIs, hardware, services, or app-specific checks. The JSON result reports signature_verified=true only after native signature verification; runtime_verified=false means the converter has not launched or tested the app. Keep decrypted apps private under the use terms above.

Convert an encrypted IPA for macOS FairPlay

This requires an encrypted IPA personalized for the same Store enrollment as your saved model. Convert it with:

./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos \
  --input App.ipa \
  --model /private/path/fairplay-enrollment.bin

Omit --model to use the saved model. The default output is App.macos.ipa. Use --output to choose another path or --force to replace an existing output.

The command uses a saved version-2 enrollment model. You can instead use a matching private 16-byte credential:

chmod 600 credential.bin
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos \
  --input App.ipa \
  --credential credential.bin

The conversion:

  • decodes the current private record with the direct enrollment model;
  • validates and rewrites the personalized SINF into the macOS layout;
  • preserves its app key, signature, rights, and other private fields;
  • adds every SINF copy declared by Apple for encrypted frameworks and extensions; and
  • leaves all Mach-O executables byte-identical and encrypted.

Model-based conversion supports the observed 440- and 448-byte private SINF records and the same bounded appended-rights geometry used by recovery.

The result is still an IPA, not a macOS installer. A macOS iOS-app wrapper or compatible installer must preserve this basic layout:

App iOS.app/
  WrappedBundle -> Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/iTunesMetadata.plist

The converted IPA and wrapper contain a private account license. Keep them private. This feature does not decrypt, modify, re-sign, or bypass checks inside the app. Apps may still reject macOS, require unavailable hardware, or depend on services that are not present on macOS.

Open encrypted IPAs in IDA Pro 9.4

The IDA archive-loader plugin offers UnfairPlay decryption when opening an encrypted IPA, discovers saved enrollment models, and loads the chosen executable with IDA's Mach-O loader. If no model exists, it shows the one-time unfairplay setup instructions. Install integrations/ida/unfairplay_ipa.py in your IDA user directory's loaders folder and make the CLI available to IDA. See the plugin guide for configuration and plaintext handling.

Open encrypted IPAs in Binary Ninja

Requires Binary Ninja 6.0.10905 or later. Run these commands from the repository root or an extracted release archive.
